newsitem.title: USA: PBS, Williams in business education venture.
newsitem.headline: PBS, Williams in business education venture.

text.p: The Public Broadcasting Service (PBS) and Williams Cos Inc said Thursday they will create "The Business Channel, LLC."

The joint venture, which builds upon PBS's seven-year-old satellite-delivered Business Channel, will use Internet, video-on-demand, fiber-optic and satellite technologies to bring professional development and training services to the business community, a statement from Williams and PBS said.
Williams is a natural gas pipeline group with a large telecommunications network.

The service is to be available by July 1, 1997. Companies signing onto it will have the capability to access 450 hours of programming on demand through an employee's desktop computer or at a company training center.
Users will not be linking up with the Internet but will access the Business Channel's computer network to tap into available programming.
The service is designed to offer a wide range of interactive training programs without forcing companies to pull employees away from their posts for extended periods of time, they said.

"The whole skills-obsolescence (quandary) businesses are facing is just stunning," said Scott McNealy, chairman, president and chief executive of Sun Microsystems Inc, which is providing computer servers for the venture. "How do you pull them off the line of fire to get them trained?"
Massachusetts Institute of Technology also is a partner, providing faculty members to help train business leaders.
Under the deal, the newly formed company will be owned equally by PBS and Williams Cos Inc. Williams Cos has agreed to spend $20 million on the service, while PBS is providing content and management.
